title: Exploratory Data Analysis
blurb: Point it at a CSV and it profiles every column — then says which are fit to model on.

steps.say: Before you model anything, you have to know what is in the data. This tool takes a CSV and works through it the way an analyst would — the shape, each column, the distributions, the correlations — and ends with a verdict on what is worth modelling.
Rather than upload anything, let's load the built-in sample. It is analysed in memory and never stored.

Here is the overview at a glance: how many rows and columns, how many duplicate rows, how much is missing, and a single data-quality score that folds those together. This is the first thing to read — a high missing rate or a pile of duplicates changes everything that follows.

Everything the analysis produced is laid out in these sections — the first rows, a per-column profile, distributions, correlations between features, and the model-fitness verdict. You can jump straight to any of them.
And the whole report exports as a standalone HTML or PDF file — the same charts and findings, in something you can hand to someone who will never open this page.

The limits, plainly: the charts are drawn from a sample of the rows, not every one, so a rare cluster can be missed; and the model-fitness call is a heuristic about each column's shape, not a promise about any particular model. It tells you where to look — the modelling is still yours.
